selected.title: Within reach
selected.texas_link: UT Austin leads the funded study of humans and robots adapting together.

movement.object: UT Austin Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation

selected.why_today: The award term began this month. Current primary sources establish an active research commitment and the tangible question it will test; this is not new funding today. The newer Docket record is a duplicate admission, not a second event.
selected.consequence: A robot that adapts its reach could help a person receive a drink within their physical limits, an aim rather than an established patient result.
selected.application_change: The planned work moves beyond completing an isolated task toward adapting assistance over repeated interactions in everyday environments.
selected.counter_image: The university pictures a mug handoff in a simulated apartment and describes adaptive reach as something a robot could learn, without care results.
selected.earned_take: Completing a handoff is only useful when the object reaches the person on their terms.

agency.next_step: Researchers plan living laboratories with communities shaping how and where deployment happens and an ethics board developing consent procedures.
agency.who_can_act: Participating communities and the research team, with no open enrollment confirmed.

rejected.title: UTA question asking tutor
rejected.reason: Strong visible teaching mechanism but its upcoming study has no learning outcomes and a narrower physical action than the selected reach problem.

rejected.title: Watershed utility cyber support
rejected.reason: Current enrollment offers no named deployed AI mechanism or measured utility outcome.
